critical_code_review_comments: routes/lead_wa_auto.py auto_wa_hot_leads(): the created_at filter uses ISO date-only string ('2026-09-27') compared against full ISO timestamps — works because the timestamp prefix compares correctly, but relies on lexicographic ordering with same-length strings. Safe today, but fragile if _now() format ever changes.
sent_today count in GET /auto-wa uses same date-prefix trick — same fragility. Consider a normalised 'created_date' field or a datetime range.

_wa_phone assumes India (+91) fallback for any 10-digit number after stripping leading 0 — international leads without country code will get mis-prefixed. OK today (India-only), but document assumption.
auto_wa_hot_leads relies on wa_intro_attempted_at + whatsapp_sent_at fields to avoid re-sends; ensure indexes on these + (created_at desc, reviews desc) for 40-lead scan to stay fast at scale.

note_lead_reply matches lead by phone-suffix regex on wa_intro_sent_at existence — if two leads share the last-10-digits (rare but possible with formatting), first match wins silently. Consider tie-breaking on most recent wa_intro_sent_at.
